messages:
mel: paging: infra-alert P99 tokens/sec drop, latency spike on hosted-us-west, paging oncall. seeing errors in the serving runtime (OOM and queue saturation).
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert triggered: serving.runtime.queue.latency.p99 > 1200ms in region hosted-us-west for 3m
mel: quick triage — is this an autoscale gap or batching pathology?
ben: logs show continuous_batcher backlog growing, queue depth up, and a flurry of small requests (seq len ~80 tokens). GPUs are spending lots of time on tiny batches.
miguel: looks like batching window is too small given current load mix. default continuous batching target_delay_ms=30 and max_batch_size=32. throughput suffers when we have many short requests and spike fanout.
sara: customer impact — a few mid-tier customers on hosted are reporting 500s and partial streams. I opened a ticket with CSM for affected tenants.
mel: mitigation plan proposal: 1) increase target_delay to favor aggregation (trade latency for throughput), 2) tighten per-key rate limiting to reduce tiny-request churn, 3) disable streaming for a short canary to reduce kernel-switch overhead. Execute in that order.
ben: agree. propose commands:
```
# increase batching delay across hosted-us-west runtime
redwoodctl apply --region=hosted-us-west --patch '{"runtime": {"continuous_batcher": {"target_delay_ms": 120, "max_batch_size": 64}}}' --reason "emergency throughput mitigation"
# tighten per-key token bucket for public-tier to 10 rps
redwoodctl rate-limit set --scope=hosted-us-west --policy public-tier --rps 10
# temporarily disable streaming for small responses
redwoodctl feature toggle set --region=hosted-us-west --feature streaming.enabled --value false
```
miguel: rollouts: do the batching change as a region-wide immediate change but do the others as staged (canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%). want to observe p99 and error-rate after batching change first.
sara: CSM asked for ETA. Mel, can we give them a 30m estimate for mitigation then follow-up with concrete customer-level timeline?
mel: yes. I'll post to #customer-impact once we confirm p99 dropped.
incident-bot: action created: incident/1795023456 - owner mel - severity P1 - runbook serving/runtime/queue-saturation.md
ben: executing batching change now (kick off):
```
redwoodctl apply --region=hosted-us-west --patch '{"runtime": {"continuous_batcher": {"target_delay_ms": 120, "max_batch_size": 64}}}' --immediate
```
ben: applied. monitoring graphs up. initial effect: queue depth dropping, GPU utilization smoothing. p50 unchanged, p95 down ~30%, p99 dropping slowly.
mel: good sign. keep an eye on user-visible latency; post if any customers see regressions.
miguel: given the throughput improvement, we should also change the KV cache TTL—shortening the per-request cache check to reduce stale lookups is low-risk. I'll prepare a canary for that after we stabilize.
sara: CSM updated: two customers still experiencing intermittent 500s but fewer. they've paused heavy batch jobs on their side as we asked.
ben: next step: apply rate-limit canary to 5% of public-tier traffic to avoid knee-jerk throttling of small but legitimate bursty clients.

# canary command
redwoodctl rate-limit set --scope=hosted-us-west --policy public-tier --rps 10 --canary 5

ben: canary applied. observing for 10m. errors from backlog producers should drop.
miguel: monitoring: token refill counters show fewer tiny requests hitting the queue. memory pressure on worker pods decreasing. no OOMs in last 7m.
mel: once canary looks good, we can promote to 25% and then 100%. keep the streaming toggle off for now.

# partial rollback plan
mel: if we see customer-facing latency above 2s p95 or error rate >2% we rollback: set target_delay_ms back to 30, re-enable streaming, and lift rate-limit canary.

ben: note — some downstream integrations expect streaming; turning it off may trigger timeouts. I'm watching integration error logs. so far only a handful of retries.
sara: escalation: if this persists beyond 45m we should open a dedicated support bridge for the top 5 customers.

# 15m update
incident-bot: update: 15m elapsed since batching change. p99 latency reduced 38%. error-rate down 60%.
mel: solid. escalate canary from 5% -> 25% for rate-limit:
```
redwoodctl rate-limit set --scope=hosted-us-west --policy public-tier --rps 10 --canary 25
```
ben: canary 25% applied. continuing to monitor.
miguel: prepping a lower-risk permanent config: target_delay_ms=80 and max_batch_size=48 may be a better long-term balance. will propose in follow-up RFC.

# 35m update
incident-bot: update: 35m elapsed. p99 stable at new baseline (40% lower than baseline), error-rate low. streaming toggle remains off.
mel: start notifying customers with summary and ETA for full restore (we'll keep higher batching for throughput for 2h then reassess). Sara, send the note.
sara: posting customer note now to CSM channel.

# handoff
mel: handing off to ben for ongoing monitoring. I'll be offline for 20m starting 1795023600. Ben, keep an eye and escalate to infra oncall if p99 rises above 900ms.
ben: ack. I'll keep the incident open and update logs. next steps: promote rate-limit to 100% after 1h if stable, and schedule a rollback window 2h after that.

# incident closure note
incident-bot: incident/1795023456 status: mitigated -> monitoring. final action summary: increased continuous_batcher.target_delay_ms -> 120ms (immediate), applied staged rate-limit to public-tier (5% -> 25%), disabled streaming in hosted-us-west (temporary). owners: mel, ben, miguel.
mel: thanks team. file a short postmortem once we have metrics and cleanups to revert feature toggles and tuning.
ben: will do. adding to postmortem queue.
miguel: I'll open an RFC for a permanent batching policy that adapts target_delay by observed request size distribution.
sara: I'll follow up with CSM and affected customers with the incident summary and mitigations. :thumbsup:
